what_to_do: Confirm you qualify: not a mainland Chinese national, you work or worked in China, and you have a tax record from the Chinese tax authority showing tax paid in the last 3 years.
Open a personal Wise account and start a transfer from CNY. For the first transfer Wise verifies you, which can take 1 to 2 working days, and asks for the tax record.
Name the recipient: it must be another account you own, either a bank account outside China or your Wise account.

Pay by bank transfer from a Chinese bank account in your own name (up to 300,000 CNY per transfer) or from Alipay (up to 50,000 CNY per transfer). Money sent from an account in another name is refunded.
Repeat until you reach your overall limit. To raise it, upload further tax records when Wise prompts you.

Go to a partner bank branch (Bank of China, China Everbright Bank, Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, Postal Savings Bank of China, or one of the smaller partner banks) with your passport. Ask first whether U.S. passport holders and the United States are accepted at that branch.
Fill out the transfer details with the receiver's complete information and hand over the money and your ID. The bank may require you to hold an account with it.
Pay the transfer fee and keep the receipt with the Money Transfer Control Number (MTCN).
Give the MTCN only to your receiver, who collects the cash at a Western Union agent location abroad.

Settle which rule lets you convert, using the route on the main dashboard that matches where the money came from. Banks ask for supporting documents: Agricultural Bank's page says so for amounts above its daily threshold.
Ask the branch for its selling rate for your amount on the day, in writing. The published board is a reference only; the transaction rate is what you get.
Buy the dollars into your own foreign-currency account (现汇, not 现钞). A cash-to-wire conversion fee applies only if the account holds banknotes.
Send one wire for the whole amount to your own U.S. account. Every bank read here caps its fee per wire, so splitting multiplies the fee.
Choose the shared (SHA) charge option unless you need the full amount to arrive. Under OUR, China Merchants Bank pre-charges USD 25 or more.
Submit on a working day: China Construction Bank processes 9:00 to 17:00, ICBC 9:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday.
Expect a receiving fee in the U.S.: USD 15 at Bank of America and at Chase.
